S19.title: The Pool. Nick Without the Perfect Shot

paragraphs.S19.C000.P000: By the entrance, Nick held his phone up for Alice to see: the schedule said the pool was open until nine today, on a weekday.
paragraphs.S19.C000.P001: “The last hour is open. If we spend it discussing whether to go, it will be a very modern date.”
paragraphs.S19.C000.P003: “I can rename it. ‘A joint assessment of water temperature.’”
paragraphs.S19.C000.P004: Alice laughed and stopped by the door. A bag hung from his shoulder, with a camera strap sticking out.
paragraphs.S19.C000.P005: “You said you would leave it in the room.”
paragraphs.S19.C000.P006: Nick looked at the strap as if it had only just grown there.
paragraphs.S19.C000.P007: “There's a towel in the bag too. I took the camera out... wait.”
paragraphs.S19.C000.P008: He unzipped it. The camera really was inside. Alice's irritation did not disappear because he was honestly surprised.
paragraphs.S19.C000.P009: “You picked it up out of habit,” she said.
paragraphs.S19.C000.P010: “Yes. I'll take it back. You can go in and wait; you can come with me. Five minutes.”
paragraphs.S19.C000.P011: “I'll wait here. And if we go in, no filming.”
paragraphs.S19.C000.P013: He walked away quickly and returned without the bag, but with a towel wrapped around his neck like an absurd scarf. He did not use a long joke to save himself from the mistake.
paragraphs.S19.C000.P014: They went separate ways in the changing rooms. Alice reached the outdoor pool first. The locals spoke quietly; no one cared who had come from far away or why. October's sky was darkening over the water. The water was warm enough to make her gradually forget the cold of the walks, but not warm enough to dissolve her thoughts.
paragraphs.S19.C000.P015: Nick appeared with wet hair, looked around, and waved to her from the other side of the pool. He did not rush straight over. Alice swam to the edge where he had his palms on the tiles.
paragraphs.S19.C000.P016: “If you ask what I look like without a camera, I'll answer honestly,” she warned.
paragraphs.S19.C000.P017: “I was going to ask who designed this ladder. But now I'm interested in the answer.”
paragraphs.S19.C000.P018: “You look like someone who forgot his glasses and is too proud to squint.”
paragraphs.S19.C000.P019: He laughed. A few minutes later Nick suggested a game: each of them had to invent an impossible title for a film about their day. His was “The Man Who Defeated the Zip.” Alice called hers “Eight Minutes No One Will Get.” Nick did not ask who the film was for. He simply remembered the title.
paragraphs.S19.C000.P020: A lane opened at the far end of the pool. Alice suggested they swim to it without racing, but Nick immediately asked what prize came with second place. Halfway there, he lost his rhythm, stopped, and let her go ahead. She touched the wall first and looked back. He swam slowly, without any show of ease, his brows drawn together with stubborn concentration. She waited until he reached her, without turning the pause into a reason to rescue him.
paragraphs.S19.C000.P021: “You can say I lost,” Nick panted.
paragraphs.S19.C000.P023: “Then why was I trying so hard?”
paragraphs.S19.C000.P025: He swam a few metres away from the edge and lay on his back. Alice did the same. Dark air stretched above them; splashing came from the next lane, and steam rose from the water before disappearing without covering the lights. Nick admitted that in water he always tried to look confident because, as a child, he had started lessons later than all his friends. He did not tell a story about injury or heroic overcoming—he simply showed how his left hand lost its rhythm when he hurried. Alice tried swimming beside him more slowly, at his pace. This time he reached the end without stopping. They both climbed out pleased not by the result, but by the fact that they could look awkward and still stay beside each other.
paragraphs.S19.C000.P026: Then the game ended by itself. Alice rested the back of her head against the wall. Nick said it was hard for him to leave days without an image. Not because every day was good; the opposite—bad days could be rebuilt. Put the morning joke before the evening silence, and you got a person who had always managed.
paragraphs.S19.C000.P027: “I know it's unfair,” he said. “Sometimes editing feels kinder than memory.”
paragraphs.S19.C000.P030: He did not add the story about failure he had already told her at the lagoon, and he did not ask for comfort. Alice remembered how he had first said the word “afraid” there without a smile. Today he was trying to sit with the word for longer than a second.
paragraphs.S19.C000.P031: “If you cut everything from our trip where we are silent,” she said, “I won't recognise either you or me in it.”
paragraphs.S19.C000.P032: “Then I won't decide for you which pieces stay.”
paragraphs.S19.C000.P033: “Is that a promise for the film?”
paragraphs.S19.C000.P035: When they came out, the window in the small lobby reflected two elongated shadows. Nick stopped.
paragraphs.S19.C000.P036: The administrator was looking for a lost locker bracelet. A guest remembered its number from a photograph, but his phone had died. Nick had already raised a hand toward his pocket as if a camera were there, then lowered it. Together with Alice, he walked along the benches. Alice found the bracelet under a rolled towel. The guest thanked them; Nick was more embarrassed than she was.
paragraphs.S19.C000.P037: “Without a shot, no one will believe in our rescue operation,” he whispered.
paragraphs.S19.C000.P038: “I will confirm the locker number under oath.”
paragraphs.S19.C000.P039: While they put on their shoes, Nick told her how he had once edited a funny scene out of someone else's confusion. The person laughed during the screening, then asked him to remove it the next day. Nick did, but remembered his first irritation. Alice did not praise him for deleting it. For the first time, he finished the story without a joking escape hatch.
paragraphs.S19.C000.P040: “It would be funny to film only the shadows now,” he said. “No faces, no publication. But I don't have my phone. I can go get it if you want. Or we can keep this ours.”
paragraphs.S19.C000.P041: She could see how much he wanted to catch the image. She liked that he had asked before taking out the phone. And she disliked that the question had arisen at all. They were two different feelings, and neither required her to cancel the other immediately.

S19.C001.title: Choice S19-C1 — Who gets the reflection

S19.C002.title: A. Take the shadows on Alice's phone

paragraphs.S19.C002.P000: “On mine,” Alice said. “One picture. It stays with me until I decide otherwise.”
paragraphs.S19.C002.P002: She took out her phone and pointed it at the glass. Nick stepped half a pace away so that only the reflections would be in the frame, and asked whether he could come back. She nodded. The picture held two uneven figures and a bright sign between them.
paragraphs.S19.C002.P003: “The worst advertisement for romance,” Nick said.
paragraphs.S19.C002.P005: She put the phone away without sending him the picture. Nick did not ask for a copy.

S19.C003.title: B. Do not take a picture at all

paragraphs.S19.C003.P001: Nick raised his hands as if he were releasing an invisible camera.
paragraphs.S19.C003.P002: “Then I'll need another proof that we were here.”
paragraphs.S19.C003.P005: They bought a glass of water in the lobby and watched the reflections break apart whenever someone passed. Nick did not repeat the offer. On the way back, he invented a title for the missing shot and asked Alice to remember it instead of recording it.

S19.C004.title: C. Suggest taking a picture tomorrow in daylight, if they both want to

paragraphs.S19.C004.P000: “Not now,” Alice said. “Ask again tomorrow in daylight. I might want to take your picture myself.”
paragraphs.S19.C004.P001: Nick smiled broadly, then the smile became smaller and more serious.
paragraphs.S19.C004.P005: They left the shadows behind the glass. Tomorrow's “maybe” remained a question.

paragraphs.S19.C005.P000: On the way back from the pool, music drifted from another car past an empty shop window. Nick caught the rhythm, made two ridiculous steps, and held out a hand to Alice, palm up.
paragraphs.S19.C005.P001: “My film is going through a difficult time. Maybe at least a dance?”
paragraphs.S19.C005.P002: Alice took his hand. Nick stepped too wide, caught the kerb with his shoe, and laughed at himself before she could worry. She moved him onto the dry asphalt and counted a slow beat. The music drove away with the car; they made the last two steps in silence.
paragraphs.S19.C005.P003: “I thought that if I didn't film it, I'd forget,” Nick said.
paragraphs.S19.C005.P004: “You'll forget part of it. So will I.”
paragraphs.S19.C005.P006: “Sometimes I like that it is impossible to show everything to everyone else.”
paragraphs.S19.C005.P007: He looked at her without his usual ready-made line.

S19.C006.title: Choice S19-C2 — How will Alice respond to the closeness

S19.C007.title: A. Offer him a kiss herself

paragraphs.S19.C007.P001: “Yes. Wait, I'm not joking right now.”
paragraphs.S19.C007.P002: He moved closer only after she did. His hair still smelled of the pool. When they parted, Nick was the first to speak:
paragraphs.S19.C007.P005: He walked her to the guesthouse door without turning the kiss into a scene about two winners.

S19.C008.title: B. Hug him and leave the evening without a kiss

paragraphs.S19.C008.P000: “Hug me if you want,” Alice said. “We'll stop there.”
paragraphs.S19.C008.P001: Nick asked once more with his eyes; she nodded. He hugged her over her jacket, firmly and briefly.
paragraphs.S19.C008.P002: “I'm always looking for the final shot,” he admitted.
paragraphs.S19.C008.P003: “An evening has a door. That's enough.”
paragraphs.S19.C008.P004: He let go before she asked him to, and they went into the house separately.

paragraphs.S19.C009.P000: “Right now I want to walk the rest alone,” Alice said.
paragraphs.S19.C009.P002: “Then I'll come in a couple of minutes. You don't have to explain.”
paragraphs.S19.C009.P003: “I don't want you to think the pool was a mistake.”
paragraphs.S19.C009.P004: “I don't. And neither was your answer.”
paragraphs.S19.C009.P005: She walked ahead, hearing his steps behind her only as far as the corner where he really did stop.

paragraphs.S19.C010.P000: On day ten, Nick sent Alice a message from the next room: “I remember the film title. I won't write it here or ruin the experiment.” She smiled, but did not have to answer. Over breakfast with the group, he talked about bread, the forecast, and a spoon someone had forgotten. He did not use their evening as a joke for everyone else.

S19.C011.title: S19-P-A — after the picture of the shadows on Alice's phone

paragraphs.S19.C011.P000: Nick asked Alice to show him the picture without taking the phone from her hands. “Yesterday the sign split us in half,” he said. Alice noticed it only now. The picture stayed in her gallery; Nick did not have it.

paragraphs.S19.C012.P000: Nick asked whether she remembered the title of their unfilmed movie. Alice deliberately mixed up two words; he corrected her and laughed. No one wrote the title down.

S19.C013.title: S19-P-C — after suggesting they ask in the morning

paragraphs.S19.C013.P000: Nick asked again over breakfast whether she still wanted to take the picture. Alice answered, “Not today. I like that you asked again.” He said “Okay” and pushed a plate of bread toward her. The phone stayed in his pocket.
paragraphs.S19.C013.P001: Nick's editing file froze during the day. The screen held a shot of Alice at the lagoon, turned away from the lens. He called her over to decide whether to keep it. She asked him to delete it from the working sequence. “The wind comes through well,” Nick began, heard himself, and pressed delete. There was another shot for the wind: an empty path. She stayed beside him while the programme saved the project.
paragraphs.S19.C013.P002: That evening, when Alice entered the kitchen, the laptop screen was closed. Nick asked whether she wanted tea.

paragraphs.S19.C014.P000: Nick put tea on the table and sat opposite her. “I meant it yesterday,” he said quietly. Alice answered, “I remember.” Later he sent her a list of shots he wanted to show the group, so she could mark her presence in advance.

paragraphs.S19.C015.P000: Nick put a piece of paper with the impossible film title beside her cup. Alice tucked it into her notebook. “No final shot today?” she asked. “Today I'm saving the draft,” he answered, and went to get the towels.

paragraphs.S19.C016.P000: Nick asked from the doorway whether he could come into the kitchen, where Alice was already sitting. She said yes: yesterday's wish to walk alone did not turn the shared table into a ban. He took the window seat and asked about tea without moving closer to her chair.

paragraphs.S19.C017.P000: By evening, the clothes were dry and the backpacks stood by the doors. Morning of day 11 — S22.

S19.C018.title: Choice S19-C3 — What will Alice suggest to Nick after their evening together?

S19.C019.title: A. Spend part of tomorrow without cameras

paragraphs.S19.C019.P000: “I want to see the town with you, not on your screen,” Alice said. Nick put the camera in his bag and said he knew a good bakery. He invited her there before the group left.

S19.C020.title: B. Find the place with the most unusual local breakfast

paragraphs.S19.C020.P000: Alice suggested that she and Nick visit a small café they had not tried. He started reading reviews, but she stopped him. “Let's just look.” They chose a place by the smell of fresh bread coming through the open door.
